title: Detect Duplicate Transactions
statement:
A payment system records `n` transactions, numbered `0` to `n - 1` in the order they were recorded. Transaction `i` has a `sender`, a `receiver`, an `amount` and a `timestamp`.

Two transactions are **duplicates of each other** if they have the **same sender, the same receiver and the same amount, but different timestamps**. (Two records that agree on all four fields are not duplicates of each other.)

A transaction is **flagged** if it is a duplicate of at least one other transaction. Print the indices of all flagged transactions in increasing order. If no transaction is flagged, print `-1`.

Sender and receiver names are case-sensitive.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains `sender receiver amount timestamp`, where `sender` and `receiver` are strings and `amount` and `timestamp` are integers.
outputFormat: Print the 0-indexed indices of the flagged transactions in increasing order, separated by single spaces, or `-1` if there are none.
constraints: `sender` and `receiver` consist of 1 to 10 lowercase letters

examples.input:
5
alice bob 100 10
alice bob 100 25
carol bob 100 10
alice bob 100 10
bob alice 100 30
examples.explanation: Transactions 0, 1 and 3 all go from alice to bob with amount 100, and they do not all share the same timestamp (10, 25, 10). Transaction 0 and 1 differ in timestamp, as do 1 and 3, so all three are flagged. Transactions 2 and 4 have a unique (sender, receiver, amount) combination.

examples.input:
3
a b 5 1
a b 5 1
a b 6 2
examples.explanation: Transactions 0 and 1 agree on every field including the timestamp, so they are not duplicates of each other. Transaction 2 has a different amount.
